page: Amazon Web Services c7g.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro System. Hardware resources include 8 dedicated physical cores based on the 64-bit arm64 ARMv8 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz. Operating without simultaneous multithreading, each core executes a single thread, complemented by 64 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 16.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB per core ratio typical of compute-oriented systems. The instance features hardware AES support but excludes x86-specific vector extensions. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 4 Gbps. The c7g.2xlarge does not include local disk storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

Benchmark evaluations place the instance predominantly in the midtier category across general computation and memory subsystems. Stress-ng scores show 1532.98 for single-core and 12238.41 for multi-core performance, mirrored by Geekbench results of 1473 single-core and 8116 multi-core scores. Memory bandwidth achieves 146.42 GB/sec for large sequential reads and 63.37 GB/sec for large writes. Clang compilation yields a Geekbench score of 11625, while Redis operations reach 13.27 million operations per second, and static web serving delivers 15.45 GB/sec. Conversely, the system exhibits lower relative throughput in bzip3 decompression, registering 7.55 GB/sec single-threaded and 35.95 GB/sec multi-threaded, alongside a weak PassMark encryption score of 1114.02 and poor 7B LLM prompt processing at 14.13 tokens per second.

From an architectural efficiency standpoint, the c7g.2xlarge provides predictable performance due to its fully dedicated non-hyperthreaded physical cores and high memory bandwidth per core. The absence of integrated local storage necessitates attaching remote block storage, introducing external latency for I/O-intensive workloads. Given the 1:2 memory ratio and competitive CPU throughput per resource unit, this instance is suitable for web serving, microservices, container orchestration, Clang-based continuous integration builds, and general compute-heavy application tiers that do not demand accelerated GPU compute or expansive memory footprints.
description: Amazon Web Services c7g.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit arm64 AWS Graviton ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 architecture. The configuration supplies 8 dedicated physical CPU cores running at 2.6 GHz with one thread per core, paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 compute-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes 32 MB of L3 cache, hardware AES cryptographic acceleration, and 4 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. No local storage or hardware GPUs are bundled with this instance type. In benchmark testing, the instance achieves midrange performance across multi-core compute workloads, Clang software compilation, Redis operations, and memory bandwidth, while exhibiting weaker results in bzip3 decompression, PassMark encryption, and LLM prompt processing. The c7g.2xlarge is suited for microservices, application servers, software compilation pipelines, and containerized compute tasks that benefit from dedicated non-hyperthreaded ARM cores without requiring local NVMe storage.
